question: Should OpenClaw add task-level model metadata to `HEARTBEAT.md`, or should this use case be handled through cron jobs, a broader routing hook, or plugin policy instead?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing, but the safe implementation depends on maintainer intent for public syntax, split-versus-batched execution, provider/model allowlists, fallback/auth behavior, and session-state ownership.

options.title: Design shared heartbeat routing contract
options.body: Keep the issue open and decide a reusable heartbeat task routing contract that covers syntax, grouping/splitting, fallback/auth, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Add narrow heartbeat task metadata
options.body: Accept a focused `HEARTBEAT.md` task `model` field and implement explicit execution semantics plus compatibility tests for mixed-model due tasks.

options.title: Use cron or plugin routing instead
options.body: Decline new heartbeat task syntax and document that model-specific periodic work should use cron per-job models or a plugin routing policy, with the limitation that `HEARTBEAT.md` tasks stay run-level.

recommendation.title: Design shared heartbeat routing contract
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and decide a reusable heartbeat task routing contract that covers syntax, grouping/splitting, fallback/auth, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest likely owner for the model-routing product boundary and already appears in adjacent hook and heartbeat provenance.
